title: Good feedback needs a home. — Cynthia Udoh
description: A practical argument for one clear place to make decisions. A practical project management field note by Cynthia Udoh.

section_01.text_006: Cynthia Udoh · 1 min read · Portfolio editorial draft
section_01.text_009: THE PRACTICE OF MOVING WORK FORWARD

section_03.text_002: One comment arrives in a call. Another sits under an old design link. A third appears in a direct message. Before anyone can make the change, someone has to find the comments, compare them, and work out which decision is current.
section_03.text_004: Bring feedback into one agreed place and connect it to the right version of the work. This does not mean every conversation must happen in one tool. It means the final direction should be easy to find.
section_03.text_006: “Make this stronger” tells the team very little. Is the hierarchy unclear? Is the message missing a key point? Does the page ask the visitor to do too many things? Describing the problem gives the person doing the work room to solve it thoughtfully.
section_03.text_008: When two comments pull in different directions, do not quietly pass both to the team. Identify the conflict, ask the right decision-maker, and record the answer. That small pause can prevent an unnecessary cycle of revisions.
section_03.text_010: When a round of feedback has been addressed, summarize the changes and name the questions that remain open. A review becomes easier when everyone understands what they are being asked to evaluate.
